Two hours late, it seems.
If you finished the 8th reset before, or enter Christmalloween now, you miss Arms Bent Back. Though, if you triggered it at some point between the reset and installing this update, you'll be fine.
A bug in the second Nodokathon where Genesis 19 (Pillars of Salt) gave Floor 1 a point is fixed and now the point goes to Floor 2.
In replays, Pen & Paper now starts with tokimekilabyrinth.mp3 instead of tsukiokamanor.mp3.
The Chika maid cafe generic is now only accessible if, besides AKIRA NOT BEING A FUCKING PUSSY, Chika isn't broken.
The first Dorm Wars now also needs you to either have rejected Sara, or to have seen She's Always a Woman.
Now, to see ASS, besides the other conditions, you need to have seen Practice Makes Perfect, which now also needs you to have seen Hello Alone.

And probably other things I missed. Now, for the update itself.
Just one big event chain. Deer God, if I understand this correctly, you need to either have seen or missed a certain number of events for each character, and at least 104 events of Chapter 4 if I'm reading this correctly.
That's right, not certain events, but a number of events, either seen or missed.

Starts on Friday as long as you fulfill the conditions.
You miss a Sara event if you missed the second Nodokathon.

posts.content_html_raw:
I had fun with this Dorm Wars.

I won’t pretend it was super mindblowing or anything, but it was nice to venture back into Kumon-mi after two months of no real updates.

My rating? I’d give it a 7/10. Just a good, well-rounded update. And that’s all it needs to be.

Could we actually be in for a reward for the Dorm Wars outcome this time?? It seems heavily implied to be the case, but then again, so was the sleepover at Sensei’s house in Dorm Wars 2, so I won’t believe it ‘till I see it.

Sana and Sara actually had a threesome together, huh? I’m… very conflicted about this. Part of me feels bad for Sara, but then the other just finds it super hot…

Ah, who am I kidding. Bring on more of the wincest.

That said, though, I’m still really sus about Sana. Even Ayane and Sara at the cafe were skeptical of her behavior. Like… part of me thinks this isn’t actually her. Or… is her physically, just with an artificially warped personality. Again, due to the “Perfect Harmony” triple moon shenanigans on the Beach way back when. Or during the 0.45 reset. You know, when there was three separate timelines going on?

Who’s to say that shit ever got fully resolved? Who’s to say a lot of things aren’t just an illusion or some construct of Pareidolia’s design?

I just can’t buy his sob story when he left Sensei before. Why should we ever take a god at their word about anything?

Hell, he’s still messing with Yumi’s head in this very update.

His host may have changed, but have his intentions?

We’re still in the Infinite Spring for a reason…

Or hey, maybe I’m just wrong entirely and I’m just massively overthinking it. That certainly wouldn’t surprise me either.

The Niki and Maya conversation was a long time coming, and from what we got of it, I enjoyed it. I definitely think it could have gone on a tad longer, though. It was more focused on setup than anything, so it’ll be awhile until we get to see the payoff.

Oh, and speaking of Niki and conversations, I’m so glad she gave Chika that wakeup call. It was brutal and blunt, no doubt, but if it can finally snap her out of this Crazy Arc at long last? I’ll take it, man.

Sorry to jump back to the Sana/Sara threesome again, but… what was up with those text messages at the end? Who was it? What did it mean?

Am I missing some subtle detail? Or is this just something we’re gonna be in the dark about for a couple more months?

I really enjoyed that small Nodokathon 2.5 event with all the girls in their lingerie. They all looked amazing.

Who did you guys pick? I saw the hidden Nodoka choice locked behind an affection requirement, but… I went with Otoha. Mainly because… I dunno. I guess I just really like Otoha lately.

She’s miles more interesting to me than she was in Chapter 2 and 3. A lot like Osako. Chapter 4 has done a lot for their development.

Speaking of Otoha… it seems she kind of has a small thing going with Tsukasa? Maybe?

Wonder if that’ll ever go anywhere.

Ayane remembered Himawari once again at the end of the trivia. That was the same food she always ate and Ayane said it wasn’t nutritious enough. Easy to forget if the Aomori section isn’t fresh in your mind, but I got it.

Oh yeah, then later in the update at Koi Cafe, Ayane tells Sara about the ‘strange dream’ she had. Perhaps about Himawari?

Hm… What else…?

Oh yeah. Imani, I know you wanna give Akira the benefit of the doubt, but come on. Surely she… knows, doesn’t she?

I mean, the writing’s kinda on the wall.

Maybe the utterly hilarious curse of getting caught fucking at the Beach will continue and Imani walks in on it. What would she do then, I wonder?

So yeah. Fun update. 7/10. Can’t wait to get back to it in July.

posts.content_html_raw:
The point (to my understanding) is to provide a play-by-play live commentary on the events, that's why he prefaces each part with "event x", following the convention provided by the trigger guide.

The intended experience is for you to imagine having Yarazin talking at your side as you both read through the events.

If this works for someone or not, or if they're even the intended audience for this sort of visceral reaction is another topic. It reminds me a lot about how I'd comment on manhua chapters with my gut, and often extreme, reactions and a lot of people would be pissed at me for them.

The merits of such reactions is that they are not toned down or organized, they're not even logical a lot of the times.
Were I (or him in this case) to talk about the same chapter I commented on after organizing my thoughts, there would be a revision on what I thought, if not many - and my post would become something more akin to a review, rather than a reaction.

Different strokes.

You remember Nu Maya has already died correctly, do you remember the same has happened to Nodoka and Makoto? Ami from the end of Ch3 too? Pareidolia offers to bring her back in exchange for raping Karin, which he refuses to do. Noriko brings up the fact this is a similar memory issue to what Sensei has, which puts him on the path of trying to do so. She then hears Maya's dialogue during her rooftop sex before meeting a crying Maya sitting at a desk, it's definitely supposed to be Prime, but I don't know if that's how she's constantly being kept prisoner or if she was just created for that TSS. Makoto informs Nu Maya of her memory loss in a way that actually gets to her. 0.46's best event is them talking about what Prime was and what Nu Maya is going to turn into if she keeps going. Very explicitly, Nao more than ever ends with Maya Makinami's Sentience score increasing by 1 after an event where Nao tries but fails to have Maya start asking the right questions. 0.53 explains that Prime created this time looped world with a wish and 0.54 shows Nu Maya not being able to comprehend that fact, which was teased again just now in 0.58. Maya getting her memories back is a central theme to Ch4, we can't fix the world until we understand it and the only person who is going to know that is Maya Prime.

Now going into theory territory, thematically it would make most sense for Maya to get her memories back at the end of Ch4 and make Ch4's length span the amount of time she lost them for. The game doesn't just end when Prime gets her memories back it's not like we know how to end the problem we just need an admin password only Prime knew. Whatever we need to do to end the loop we can only start preparing for it once Prime explains the world and the wish used to create it, as well as what she knows or thinks she knows about things. Wires supposed death after her early game hints about not liking HOPE are also things that will slow down the resolution so we have enough time for more content with her before Dark Route. There's also. There were also threads before her reset that need to be finished (the rest of that Loli Maya crying on top of Sensei, the naked Maya standing at the end of that weird school hallway) and personally I think it'd just be a bit shit if those were moved to Maya's purity route when the others are going to be dedicated to their happy ending.You'd also miss out on the golden opportunity for Prime to have to deal with the consequences of Nu Maya not sticking to the stoic script. Now she has to at the very least deal with the fact that Otoha was jerking a buttplug she was wearing in front of other girls in the class and Sensei. Imagine if she says she loves him in front of the other girls. What if Prime then tries to say she loves him once she returns and Sensei blacks out?

Things are already busy enough that I don't think spring is wrapping up this cycle, in fact it's now explicit that whoever are in the USER accounts right now are currently fighting for control. We don't know if USER4 was Himawari being useful, or some other entity (Janitor Sekai?) but I imagine come the reset at the beach trip (if November is to be a break like was just mentioned) that some god will be in control afterward and will start speaking to Akira again. We've also got to see what Pareidolia's doing with Yumi before all things are said and done. If you've been following me you might know I have a specific theory of how chapter 4 might come full circle, and with Otoha showing up in her underwear for this nodokathon lite I'm very invested in her upcoming 3 event chain and whether that theory thrives or dies for it.

posts.content_html_raw:
And so another Dorm War comes to an end!

I think this one has been perhaps my favorite so far, truth be told. The events were fresh enough that it didn't feel repetitive, the characters all got to have fun times, especially my favorites.

Plenty of stand out moments throughout the update!

I'll lead with the most obvious two:

Nodokathon 2.5...and the threesome.

Nodokathon 2.5 was GREAT. Character interactions in ways they never have before, learning new things not just about themselves but eachother. Nodoka truly outdid herself this time. I mentioned it earlier...but I kinda had forgotten that Otoha was "hot". She's been such a non-entity since her and Rin broke up that she's just been a background character with a great theme song. But when she shows up here? Wow.

Maya was cute, tail plug interaction with Otoha was peak.

Chika was quite sane for once.

Tsuneyo was banging. Sensei needs to get this one figured out!

I picked Nodoka for the win as she is one of my favorites, and I think having the balls to continue putting together filth for Akira should be rewarded.



Sana was, as always, the perfect bratty sub. Akira should fall in love with her more.

Sara was a surprise. I don't know 100% that she was 100% into it...but if not, she is a fantastic actress.

Either way, in Akira's shoes, I'm folding for the tag team as well. 10/10, getting eloped, no further notes here.



Other Moments:

Tsukasa is once again hilariously precocious. Her telling Otoha she would make alot of money acting in porn was hysterical.

Truthfully, I think the writing in this update, while not impactful emotionally for the most part...was really well written from a humor aspect. I laughed alot more this time around than I have for a good few updates. Plenty of plot points came together as well, which I appreciated. Also, maybe Chika is finally cured of her rabies and can go back to being a hot little filipina fuck doll? One can only hope. Chinami needs her big sister back before she dies of something that could have been stopped by having a functional guardian.

I did, however, love the Maya/Niki talk.

Maya Prime was such a hard ass character, that while you grow to love her, you don't really get much depth from her beyond the fact that she's been trapped in a timeloop for thousands of years, and loves Akira but can't love him the way she wants.

Nu Maya, though? We get to see the depths of her emotions, the way she sees akira is different from everyone else. That she recognizes the good in him, is, I think, very important here. Well, that was a very solid update. An easy 8, although I didn't like that they cut certain parts of the events, like Nikki and Maya's conversation or the call/message at the end of the trio scene with Sara and Sana. I understand it's to generate mystery for the next update, but it was still annoying.
The best part? Nikki, without a doubt, especially her conversations with Rin and Chikka. Regarding the latter, I initially thought Nikki was being a bit cruel to Chikka, but I understood that it was precisely what she needed to free herself from her madness, so I'm grateful that, apparently, we'll have the old Chikka back.
Then there was the encounter with Maya, and it didn't disappoint me at all, being one of the encounters I was most looking forward to. If I had to find a complaint, it would be that it felt too short, for the reasons I mentioned at the beginning. To conclude, I would say that both girls showed us that they have not only opposing but antagonistic views of what love is, and that ironically they share these views with their two other rivals, albeit separately.

An easy 8, although I didn't like that they cut certain parts of the events, like Nikki and Maya's conversation or the call/message at the end of the trio scene with Sara and Sana. I understand it's to generate mystery for the next update, but it was still annoying.
The best part? Nikki, without a doubt, especially her conversations with Rin and Chikka. Regarding the latter, I initially thought Nikki was being a bit cruel to Chikka, but I understood that it was precisely what she needed to free herself from her madness, so I'm grateful that, apparently, we'll have the old Chikka back.
Then there was the encounter with Maya, and it didn't disappoint me at all, being one of the encounters I was most looking forward to. If I had to find a complaint, it would be that it felt too short, for the reasons I mentioned at the beginning. To conclude, I would say that both girls showed us that they have not only opposing but antagonistic views of what love is, and that ironically they share these views with their two other rivals, albeit separately.

I fully concur that Niki is absolutely the best part of 0.58 (which was… kind of expected, to be honest, since this event chain was very obviously centered around her, judging just by the name alone), and I think that one of the most interesting things about her character that we only really saw occasional glimpses of before, but truly came to the forefront in this particular update is the stark difference in, let’s just say, maturity between how “real Niki” – meaning Niki outside of her idol persona – interacts with Akira (and, to a lesser extent, Noriko) vs how she interacts with everyone else.

Ever since her introduction all the way back in Chapter 2, Niki’s most defining character traits have always been “haughty”, “controlling” and “quick to anger”. This is how she was presented to us in “What Was”, and, likewise, this is how she generally acts in most of the events she’s in: like an extremely bossy, rude and arrogant control freak with anger management issues – especially during the scenes where she is either directly talking to Akira or bringing him up in a conversation with someone else (which makes sense, considering that he is the primary reason why Niki has developed those personality traits in the first place), though she also behaves like that with Otoha during their private tutoring sessions, not to mention many, many examples of Niki’s unprofessional/borderline abusive behavior towards her co-workers, so it’s hard to blame *all* of it on just Akira.

Now, obviously, there is much more to her character than just her negative qualities: Niki is absolutely capable of being gentle, caring, selfless, protective and so on when the need arises (perfectly exemplified by her Chapter 3 event chain where she guides Sensei through his old memories and helps him remember his name), so the she is far from being boring or one-dimensional – but for the most part it *is* true that the vast, vast majority of interactions between these two characters consistently follow the same exact pattern of Akira being a pathetic little bitch and Niki acting like an immature cunt queen who feels the need to ascertain her superiority over him every three seconds (unless they are having sex, in which case their positions are explicitly reversed).

This also extends to how she treats Noriko – for the most part, anyway – both due to the girl being her little sister and due to the specifics of how Noriko is directly involved in Niki’s insane clusterfuck of a relationship with Akira (*especially* after what happened in 0.50), and the last five-six updates very much established that Niki herself is completely mentally deranged when it comes to her sorry excuse of a childhood boyfriend, to the point where Akira’s stunt in “Say Anything” actually fucking worked because… Stockholm Syndrome, I guess, despite the fact that literally *any* other woman with even a modicum of self-respect and/or self-preservation would have told him to fuck off and never approach her again.

I bring all of this up to directly highlight Niki’s very… fluctuating levels of mental maturity in relation to everything concerning Akira/Noriko, and intentionally contrast all of these examples I listed earlier with the scenes of Niki interacting with Rin, Chika and Maya in 0.58, because the difference between them is fucking astronomical.

Like, based on what happened in 0.56 (in addition to her new fun way of treating Akira like he is her property), I was fully expecting Niki to just go in completely guns blazing, verbally decimating any unfortunate teenager daring to make a claim on her man and publicly “marking her territory”, making it absolutely clear that *she* is the apex predator here and that any girl/woman deluding herself that she is in love with Sensei will first have to get through her. Or, to put it another way, my main expectation was that she would act the same way she normally does, with the ever-consistent “queen bitch” attitude towards her “competitors” that I came to strongly associate with her character.

Instead, Niki:

– Attentively listens to Rin’s personal issues and gives her genuine love advice, sharing her own very complicated experience with the subject of romance (and also takes Rin’s admission of being in love with Akira *extremely* well, to the point of… maybe not encouragement, necessarily, but at least acceptance).

– Bluntly calls out Chika on her insane obsessive behavior, actually getting through her delusional protective shell and helping the girl finally come to her senses. I especially love the fact that Niki specifically gets mad at Chika not because she is a creepy fan or a teenager sleeping with an adult man, but because the girl was ready to completely give up on Sensei after just a single demand from her role model, since even though this outcome *is* something that Niki herself ultimately wants, Chika being so wishy-washy with her feelings of love goes deeply against one of the main lessons Niki wanted to impart on her fans through her songs. It is a great inner conflict between her identity as an idol and her identity as a woman, because Niki ends up choosing the former over the latter and inadvertently pushes Chika *towards* pursuing a proper relationship with Akira, even though the initial point of this conversation was to try and dissuade her *from* doing exactly that.

– Seemingly manages to (at least partially) understand why Maya acts the way she does towards both of them, empathize with the circumstances that caused the girl to become involved with Sensei in the first place, and accept that she represents a major part of Akira’s life that Niki herself was completely unaware of (just like the earlier reveals about Sekai and Sensei’s “proclivities” from 0.50), so if she wants to truly understand Akira and potentially find a way to “heal” him, then treating Maya as yet another hormonal teenager and completely rejecting her perspective just on the basis of her age would be the *wrong* thing to do – which is why the event ends with Niki, for the lack of a better term, begrudgingly acknowledging Maya as an equal (even further compounded by the secondary realization of just how similar they actually are, which prompts Niki’s “have you ever considered becoming an idol?” question) and inviting her to continue this discussion elsewhere, while also making a token gesture of apology for making Maya’s life a living hell all these years.

All of these examples showcase a very high level of emotional and mental maturity on Niki’s part – something that she only really previously demonstrated during her attempts to be a proper mother to Ami (“Seed of Self-Doubt” probably being the most notable example, featuring a scene where Ami goes on a whole rant about herself where she indirectly admits to a lot of heinous stuff and openly says that she dislikes Niki, to which Niki just replies “do not care + did not ask + still love you and will continue to love you no matter what, even if you are an annoying incestual gremlin”) and is otherwise weirdly absent from her general characterization.

I just find it extremely curious from a narrative/writing standpoint that there is this whole deeper layer to Niki’s character that (aside from a couple rare scenes) doesn’t really get explored all that much, whether intentionally or unintentionally, because most of the events she’s in just have her primarily interact with Akira and/or Noriko – and, well, like we’ve already established, Niki is the farthest thing from “mature” when it comes to these two. I wonder if this is perhaps the reason why so many people consider her to be “boring” or “pointless”, arguing that after what happened in 0.50 Niki doesn’t really have any real reason to still play a major role in the story, and am likewise interested to know whether this approach to writing her is an unfortunate blunder on Selebus’ part or if he is steadily building towards something.

spoilers.html:
Ever since her introduction all the way back in Chapter 2, Niki’s most defining character traits have always been “haughty”, “controlling” and “quick to anger”. This is how she was presented to us in “What Was”, and, likewise, this is how she generally acts in most of the events she’s in: like an extremely bossy, rude and arrogant control freak with anger management issues – especially during the scenes where she is either directly talking to Akira or bringing him up in a conversation with someone else (which makes sense, considering that he is the primary reason why Niki has developed those personality traits in the first place), though she also behaves like that with Otoha during their private tutoring sessions, not to mention many, many examples of Niki’s unprofessional/borderline abusive behavior towards her co-workers, so it’s hard to blame *all* of it on just Akira.

Now, obviously, there is much more to her character than just her negative qualities: Niki is absolutely capable of being gentle, caring, selfless, protective and so on when the need arises (perfectly exemplified by her Chapter 3 event chain where she guides Sensei through his old memories and helps him remember his name), so the she is far from being boring or one-dimensional – but for the most part it *is* true that the vast, vast majority of interactions between these two characters consistently follow the same exact pattern of Akira being a pathetic little bitch and Niki acting like an immature cunt queen who feels the need to ascertain her superiority over him every three seconds (unless they are having sex, in which case their positions are explicitly reversed).

This also extends to how she treats Noriko – for the most part, anyway – both due to the girl being her little sister and due to the specifics of how Noriko is directly involved in Niki’s insane clusterfuck of a relationship with Akira (*especially* after what happened in 0.50), and the last five-six updates very much established that Niki herself is completely mentally deranged when it comes to her sorry excuse of a childhood boyfriend, to the point where Akira’s stunt in “Say Anything” actually fucking worked because… Stockholm Syndrome, I guess, despite the fact that literally *any* other woman with even a modicum of self-respect and/or self-preservation would have told him to fuck off and never approach her again.

I bring all of this up to directly highlight Niki’s very… fluctuating levels of mental maturity in relation to everything concerning Akira/Noriko, and intentionally contrast all of these examples I listed earlier with the scenes of Niki interacting with Rin, Chika and Maya in 0.58, because the difference between them is fucking astronomical.

Like, based on what happened in 0.56 (in addition to her new fun way of treating Akira like he is her property), I was fully expecting Niki to just go in completely guns blazing, verbally decimating any unfortunate teenager daring to make a claim on her man and publicly “marking her territory”, making it absolutely clear that *she* is the apex predator here and that any girl/woman deluding herself that she is in love with Sensei will first have to get through her. Or, to put it another way, my main expectation was that she would act the same way she normally does, with the ever-consistent “queen bitch” attitude towards her “competitors” that I came to strongly associate with her character.

Instead, Niki:

– Attentively listens to Rin’s personal issues and gives her genuine love advice, sharing her own very complicated experience with the subject of romance (and also takes Rin’s admission of being in love with Akira *extremely* well, to the point of… maybe not encouragement, necessarily, but at least acceptance).

– Bluntly calls out Chika on her insane obsessive behavior, actually getting through her delusional protective shell and helping the girl finally come to her senses. I especially love the fact that Niki specifically gets mad at Chika not because she is a creepy fan or a teenager sleeping with an adult man, but because the girl was ready to completely give up on Sensei after just a single demand from her role model, since even though this outcome *is* something that Niki herself ultimately wants, Chika being so wishy-washy with her feelings of love goes deeply against one of the main lessons Niki wanted to impart on her fans through her songs. It is a great inner conflict between her identity as an idol and her identity as a woman, because Niki ends up choosing the former over the latter and inadvertently pushes Chika *towards* pursuing a proper relationship with Akira, even though the initial point of this conversation was to try and dissuade her *from* doing exactly that.

– Seemingly manages to (at least partially) understand why Maya acts the way she does towards both of them, empathize with the circumstances that caused the girl to become involved with Sensei in the first place, and accept that she represents a major part of Akira’s life that Niki herself was completely unaware of (just like the earlier reveals about Sekai and Sensei’s “proclivities” from 0.50), so if she wants to truly understand Akira and potentially find a way to “heal” him, then treating Maya as yet another hormonal teenager and completely rejecting her perspective just on the basis of her age would be the *wrong* thing to do – which is why the event ends with Niki, for the lack of a better term, begrudgingly acknowledging Maya as an equal (even further compounded by the secondary realization of just how similar they actually are, which prompts Niki’s “have you ever considered becoming an idol?” question) and inviting her to continue this discussion elsewhere, while also making a token gesture of apology for making Maya’s life a living hell all these years.

All of these examples showcase a very high level of emotional and mental maturity on Niki’s part – something that she only really previously demonstrated during her attempts to be a proper mother to Ami (“Seed of Self-Doubt” probably being the most notable example, featuring a scene where Ami goes on a whole rant about herself where she indirectly admits to a lot of heinous stuff and openly says that she dislikes Niki, to which Niki just replies “do not care + did not ask + still love you and will continue to love you no matter what, even if you are an annoying incestual gremlin”) and is otherwise weirdly absent from her general characterization.

I just find it extremely curious from a narrative/writing standpoint that there is this whole deeper layer to Niki’s character that (aside from a couple rare scenes) doesn’t really get explored all that much, whether intentionally or unintentionally, because most of the events she’s in just have her primarily interact with Akira and/or Noriko – and, well, like we’ve already established, Niki is the farthest thing from “mature” when it comes to these two. I wonder if this is perhaps the reason why so many people consider her to be “boring” or “pointless”, arguing that after what happened in 0.50 Niki doesn’t really have any real reason to still play a major role in the story, and am likewise interested to know whether this approach to writing her is an unfortunate blunder on Selebus’ part or if he is steadily building towards something.

I fully concur that Niki is absolutely the best part of 0.58 (which was… kind of expected, to be honest, since this event chain was very obviously centered around her, judging just by the name alone), and I think that one of the most interesting things about her character that we only really saw occasional glimpses of before, but truly came to the forefront in this particular update is the stark difference in, let’s just say, maturity between how “real Niki” – meaning Niki outside of her idol persona – interacts with Akira (and, to a lesser extent, Noriko) vs how she interacts with everyone else.

Ever since her introduction all the way back in Chapter 2, Niki’s most defining character traits have always been “haughty”, “controlling” and “quick to anger”. This is how she was presented to us in “What Was”, and, likewise, this is how she generally acts in most of the events she’s in: like an extremely bossy, rude and arrogant control freak with anger management issues – especially during the scenes where she is either directly talking to Akira or bringing him up in a conversation with someone else (which makes sense, considering that he is the primary reason why Niki has developed those personality traits in the first place), though she also behaves like that with Otoha during their private tutoring sessions, not to mention many, many examples of Niki’s unprofessional/borderline abusive behavior towards her co-workers, so it’s hard to blame *all* of it on just Akira.

Now, obviously, there is much more to her character than just her negative qualities: Niki is absolutely capable of being gentle, caring, selfless, protective and so on when the need arises (perfectly exemplified by her Chapter 3 event chain where she guides Sensei through his old memories and helps him remember his name), so the she is far from being boring or one-dimensional – but for the most part it *is* true that the vast, vast majority of interactions between these two characters consistently follow the same exact pattern of Akira being a pathetic little bitch and Niki acting like an immature cunt queen who feels the need to ascertain her superiority over him every three seconds (unless they are having sex, in which case their positions are explicitly reversed).

This also extends to how she treats Noriko – for the most part, anyway – both due to the girl being her little sister and due to the specifics of how Noriko is directly involved in Niki’s insane clusterfuck of a relationship with Akira (*especially* after what happened in 0.50), and the last five-six updates very much established that Niki herself is completely mentally deranged when it comes to her sorry excuse of a childhood boyfriend, to the point where Akira’s stunt in “Say Anything” actually fucking worked because… Stockholm Syndrome, I guess, despite the fact that literally *any* other woman with even a modicum of self-respect and/or self-preservation would have told him to fuck off and never approach her again.

I bring all of this up to directly highlight Niki’s very… fluctuating levels of mental maturity in relation to everything concerning Akira/Noriko, and intentionally contrast all of these examples I listed earlier with the scenes of Niki interacting with Rin, Chika and Maya in 0.58, because the difference between them is fucking astronomical.

Like, based on what happened in 0.56 (in addition to her new fun way of treating Akira like he is her property), I was fully expecting Niki to just go in completely guns blazing, verbally decimating any unfortunate teenager daring to make a claim on her man and publicly “marking her territory”, making it absolutely clear that *she* is the apex predator here and that any girl/woman deluding herself that she is in love with Sensei will first have to get through her. Or, to put it another way, my main expectation was that she would act the same way she normally does, with the ever-consistent “queen bitch” attitude towards her “competitors” that I came to strongly associate with her character.

Instead, Niki:

– Attentively listens to Rin’s personal issues and gives her genuine love advice, sharing her own very complicated experience with the subject of romance (and also takes Rin’s admission of being in love with Akira *extremely* well, to the point of… maybe not encouragement, necessarily, but at least acceptance).

– Bluntly calls out Chika on her insane obsessive behavior, actually getting through her delusional protective shell and helping the girl finally come to her senses. I especially love the fact that Niki specifically gets mad at Chika not because she is a creepy fan or a teenager sleeping with an adult man, but because the girl was ready to completely give up on Sensei after just a single demand from her role model, since even though this outcome *is* something that Niki herself ultimately wants, Chika being so wishy-washy with her feelings of love goes deeply against one of the main lessons Niki wanted to impart on her fans through her songs. It is a great inner conflict between her identity as an idol and her identity as a woman, because Niki ends up choosing the former over the latter and inadvertently pushes Chika *towards* pursuing a proper relationship with Akira, even though the initial point of this conversation was to try and dissuade her *from* doing exactly that.

– Seemingly manages to (at least partially) understand why Maya acts the way she does towards both of them, empathize with the circumstances that caused the girl to become involved with Sensei in the first place, and accept that she represents a major part of Akira’s life that Niki herself was completely unaware of (just like the earlier reveals about Sekai and Sensei’s “proclivities” from 0.50), so if she wants to truly understand Akira and potentially find a way to “heal” him, then treating Maya as yet another hormonal teenager and completely rejecting her perspective just on the basis of her age would be the *wrong* thing to do – which is why the event ends with Niki, for the lack of a better term, begrudgingly acknowledging Maya as an equal (even further compounded by the secondary realization of just how similar they actually are, which prompts Niki’s “have you ever considered becoming an idol?” question) and inviting her to continue this discussion elsewhere, while also making a token gesture of apology for making Maya’s life a living hell all these years.

All of these examples showcase a very high level of emotional and mental maturity on Niki’s part – something that she only really previously demonstrated during her attempts to be a proper mother to Ami (“Seed of Self-Doubt” probably being the most notable example, featuring a scene where Ami goes on a whole rant about herself where she indirectly admits to a lot of heinous stuff and openly says that she dislikes Niki, to which Niki just replies “do not care + did not ask + still love you and will continue to love you no matter what, even if you are an annoying incestual gremlin”) and is otherwise weirdly absent from her general characterization.

I just find it extremely curious from a narrative/writing standpoint that there is this whole deeper layer to Niki’s character that (aside from a couple rare scenes) doesn’t really get explored all that much, whether intentionally or unintentionally, because most of the events she’s in just have her primarily interact with Akira and/or Noriko – and, well, like we’ve already established, Niki is the farthest thing from “mature” when it comes to these two. I wonder if this is perhaps the reason why so many people consider her to be “boring” or “pointless”, arguing that after what happened in 0.50 Niki doesn’t really have any real reason to still play a major role in the story, and am likewise interested to know whether this approach to writing her is an unfortunate blunder on Selebus’ part or if he is steadily building towards something.

Well I have a Niki pfp so I might be biased, but I dont think she is characterized by being a queen bitch and immature, you are leaning too far into her negative aspects. From my point of view, her role in the story is being the objectively best option for Akira at every step of the way (which, considering the topics of the game, can totally make her seem boring). Like, she is against amincest, not a teenager, is the living anchor to the few good parts of his past (instead of Maya/Noriko and Sekai->Ami), loves him unconditionally and a lot of other good qualities that would make it easy, in an ideal world, for Akira to just settle down with her and stop the madness. Even in the past she was the best option between a rapist and fucking a kid. Of course, this means she is destined to keep losing as Akira is highly traumatized AND a dumbass.

My point is that I dont find it surprising that she didnt approach this dorm wars with a "guns blazing" attitude - if so, she would have probably strangled Ami at some point in the past after the thousand incest allusions. Her trying to understand how this all came to be, and searching for the "ground zero", is pretty in line with what we have seen so far. Regardless, you are right that this whole situation will be a great opportunity to see her interact with people other than Akira, Noriko and Ami, which we have seen little of.

I bring all of this up to directly highlight Niki’s very… fluctuating levels of mental maturity in relation to everything concerning Akira/Noriko, and intentionally contrast all of these examples I listed earlier with the scenes of Niki interacting with Rin, Chika and Maya in 0.58, because the difference between them is fucking astronomical.

posts.content_html_raw:
I really had to force my way through reading this update. I think it was my least favorite in the entire game. Compared to other contenders:
  • 0.39 (sports war) had "lol so random" humor that fell completely flat, and girls went along with whatever Nodoka wanted for incredibly flimsy reasons that contradict their own characters. This update had both of those things.
  • 0.50 (Nakayarakawayama beach trip) had Niki and Sara act in completely bizarre ways that seemed to retcon previous events. This update repeated that.
0.58 had another problem beyond the above: at times, the writing itself was really, really bad, even in serious events. Like, I have no idea how something like this made it past editing:
Or how about this bundle of cliches:


Not to mention how little this feels like an actual character talking. I get there's a subtext here where Sara is trying to convince herself as much as Sensei, but it still sounds more like Selebus justifying her thought process to the reader.

A few quick thoughts on Niki:
- Did Niki ever acknowledge, even once, that grooming is a thing? She's acting like all these underage girls fell in love with Sensei and pursued him purely of their own volition. For some reason she encourages Rin and Chika's feelings without questioning where they come from. Even with Maya, who hints at how young she was, it's for some reason important to Niki that Maya "initiated" things. I expected her to have a very different reaction given what she thinks about Sekai.

- This to be in contention for dumbest line in the game:
We just got done with a whole arc where Niki was completely oblivious to things Sensei was doing in her own home, despite meeting many of the girls he was fucking. But now it just takes one look for her to figure it all out?

- I really have no idea what Selebus is trying to do with Niki's character at this point. Maya says something about her trying to find out how far Sensei has fallen to see if she can fix him, but in most of her interactions she seems very uninterested in learning. She explicitly tells Chika she doesn't care about her circumstances. It's like she's having these conversations with Rin and Chika just so she can... dispense relationship advice?

This update got me thinking about something that I think has a been a problem for a while: it often seems completely arbitrary which actions have massive consequences and which ones are completely forgotten, at least temporarily.
Many of the girls are treating Niki's instagram post and her involvement in Sensei's life like the Most Important Thing that ever happened. OK, fine, I can sort-of accept that, though it's weird that this provoked a much bigger reaction than Niki literally moving in with him (for the girls that knew about that).

But at the same time, this update was full of girls ignoring other really important things that have happened:

- Ayane and Maya are hanging out with Ami like they're all still friends and nothing's weird, even though she's been raping Maya, she made death threats to Ayane, and they both know she's "immortal". It's bizarrely out of character for Ayane to do nothing about a looming problem like this. She still hasn't even talked to Maya (that we've seen) even though it's obvious that Maya knows things that Ayane doesn't.

- Everything Nodoka has done in this game should have alienated her from the other girls: sexual harassment, sexual assault, ignoring boundaries, exposing secrets, unending condescension and self-superiority, and just never doing anything positive for anyone else. And yet, most everyone just ignores this and treats her like a normal friend/acquaintance. Sel needs victims for her to manipulate for her own storyline, so he has people go along with her for the flimsiest reasons. She's supposedly so good at manipulating people - is she really? We keep being told that, but I don't feel like we're shown it.

- During Nodokathon 2, several of the girls saw Sana do something that really can't be described as anything other than pure evil. We got one scene of them expressing mild disappointment (while ignoring Molly's own role), and then everyone went back to hanging out with her and treating her creepy perversion like it's a bit of a joke. Ayane has some concerns, but she's barely even tried to talk to Sana, much less done anything about it.

- Noriko continues to suffer no repercussions for the other way she betrayed Niki: she kept all of Sensei's crimes a secret, even as she watched her sister rebuild a relationship with a guy that Noriko knew was being unfaithful. She knows about the worst thing he's done (wizard Maya) and is still keeping that a secret, even though finding out later could potentially destroy Niki. At the very least, I would expect Noriko to struggle between her loyalty to Sensei and her loyalty to Niki, but if she feels any guilt about it the game has completely ignored it.

And this is supposed to be the same person?

Continuing the trend of us having completely different views on pretty much everything (and with the obligatory “I wholeheartedly respect your opinion, even if I strongly disagree with it” out of the way), here is an extensive list of my – hopefully, comprehensive – counterarguments to most of your criticisms (the ones that don’t firmly fall in the “entirely subjective” category, anyway, like the humor):

“We just got done with a whole arc where Niki was completely oblivious to things Sensei was doing in her own home, despite meeting many of the girls he was fucking. But now it just takes one look for her to figure it all out?”

I mean, yeah? Niki “met all of the girls he was fucking” while still firmly in denial of Akira’s true proclivities, so it makes sense that she didn’t see (or, rather, completely ignored) all of the obvious red flags due to looking at Sensei exclusively through rose-tinted glasses. The 0.50 incident, however, completely shattered these glasses, forcing Niki to actually see Akira in a semi-objective light and finally begin to notice thousands of not-so-subtle hints that he is having sex with his entire class. So, yes, I *do* fully believe that post-0.50 Niki is able to take one single look at Chika and easily connect the dots in her head, whereas previously she would have mentally excused these same signs as Chika simply being a hormonal teenager with a one-sided crush on her teacher – “because I know that Akira is better than that”.

“Many of the girls are treating Niki's instagram post and her involvement in Sensei's life like the Most Important Thing that ever happened. OK, fine, I can sort-of accept that, though it's weird that this provoked a much bigger reaction than Niki literally moving in with him (for the girls that knew about that).”

Why is it weird? Niki simply moving in with Akira is one thing, and someone looking at it from an outside perspective could potentially rationalize it to themselves in a whole number of ways: maybe these two weren’t *actually* that serious (you don’t have to be romantically involved with someone to live together, after all), or maybe this arrangement was primarily done just for Ami’s sake; and, of course, there was also the consideration of Niki’s career, making her unable, as an idol, to openly be in a proper romantic relationship with anyone – but her decision to announce to the whole world that she is now dating her childhood friend, even knowing the insane public shitstorm it would create, is an act of burning bridges that *cannot* be ignored. It indicates that Niki is 100% serious about her intentions of pursuing Akira – to the point of even being willing to readily throw away her entire career for his sake – which immediately bumps her up in the “competing for Akira’s heart” rankings of from a mythical boogieman to an active apocalyptic-level threat, so the girls’ much more extreme reaction to the Instagram post compared to the news of them actually living together makes perfect logical sense to me.

“Ayane and Maya are hanging out with Ami like they're all still friends and nothing's weird, even though she's been raping Maya, she made death threats to Ayane, and they both know she's "immortal". It's bizarrely out of character for Ayane to do nothing about a looming problem like this. She still hasn't even talked to Maya (that we've seen) even though it's obvious that Maya knows things that Ayane doesn't.”

I mean, even ignoring the fact that Ayane is still mostly mentally preoccupied with the aftermath of 0.53, constantly haunted by her lingering memories of Himawari to the point of being unable to properly focus on anything else, what *could* she even do about Ami? Talking to Sensei is out of the question (because of the explicit threat Ami made to her at the end of “The First Christmalloween”), and, to Ayane’s knowledge, no one else is actively aware of Ami’s true nature, so it’s not like she can just randomly ask Makoto (or any other member of RAS) for help with dealing with a murderous time-looper who can potentially force a Reset at any moment. Likewise, Maya is *also* currently preoccupied with her own stuff (trying to fix her deteriorating relationship with Akira, the Niki crisis, etcetera) and similarly doesn’t really have any good ideas for dealing with her “best friend”, and that is without even mentioning her weird inherent unconditional affection towards Ami (that was also shared by Maya Prime and is arguably hinted to be paranormal in nature).

Think of it this way: Ami, for all intents and purposes, is essentially an unstable time bomb – a bomb with a temporarily extinguished fuse (since, for whatever reason, she currently appears to be content with taking things slowly this cycle and just enjoying her day-to-day life to the fullest, with only some occasional “light mischief” like drugging Karin), but that is still ready to go off at a single wrong touch – and neither Maya nor Ayane really have any good ideas of how to even *begin* attempting to defuse her. So the best they can do is to kind of just… indefinitely stall for time, using this unexpected (but very welcome) lull to hopefully pacify Ami into even further inaction – especially since, once again, both girls presently have their plates full with a bunch of other personal stuff. Doing literally anything else – or, worse, actively provoking Ami – without *also* having a surefire way to deal with her if she decides to go ballistic is nothing short of suicidal, which is why their decision to continue keeping up the façade of a close-knit friend group (regardless of how these two truly feel about Arakawa junior) is a much safer and smarter approach, considering the alternatives.

“Everything Nodoka has done in this game should have alienated her from the other girls: sexual harassment, sexual assault, ignoring boundaries, exposing secrets, unending condescension and self-superiority, and just never doing anything positive for anyone else. And yet, most everyone just ignores this and treats her like a normal friend/acquaintance. Sel needs victims for her to manipulate for her own storyline, so he has people go along with her for the flimsiest reasons. She's supposedly so good at manipulating people - is she really? What makes Nodoka’s little gatherings any different?

As for her manipulation: I feel like we’ve seen plenty examples of it with just Akira alone, not to mention Yumi (“Matador”, “Things That Hurt” and “Twisting Ivy”) and Rin/Otoha (the 0.31 event chain that ends in “White-Fronted Parrot”, one of the main goals of which was to finally make those two have sex). Nodoka also managed to effortlessly navigate the mine field that is Ami after coming within an inch of being dismembered by her (Nodoka’s “How to Fuck Your Father” invite event chain), which is an achievement in and of itself, and I’m sure there are a few other instances of her playing the puppet-master that I am currently forgetting. And the Nodokathons, like I already mentioned earlier, can be mostly explained by the vast majority of the participants (with the exception of, like, Ayane for the second one, and possibly also Otoha in 0.58) being there 100% willingly, regardless of whether the reason for that is curiosity or depravity, and their personal feelings towards Nodoka herself don’t really matter in this particular case, since all of the girls are going there for *Akira*, not her: you can hate the organizer and still show up to the event itself, because the pros decidedly outweigh the cons here.

“During Nodokathon 2, several of the girls saw Sana do something that really can't be described as anything other than pure evil. So all in all, out of the six characters (among the active participants, excluding Sana herself) who are fully aware of what happened in “Thessalonians 4 (Lust Like the Pagans)”, there is essentially no one who would go as far as to completely break off their friendship with Sana just because of what she did, either because they fundamentally do not give a shit (Nodoka, Ami, Miku) or because there are extenuating circumstances that make a full-on condemnation of Sana very difficult, compared to just… continuing to occasionally hang out with her while keeping your true thoughts about the Sakakibara family to yourself (Ayane, Molly, Kirin).

spoilers.html:
“Many of the girls are treating Niki's instagram post and her involvement in Sensei's life like the Most Important Thing that ever happened. Why is it weird? Niki simply moving in with Akira is one thing, and someone looking at it from an outside perspective could potentially rationalize it to themselves in a whole number of ways: maybe these two weren’t *actually* that serious (you don’t have to be romantically involved with someone to live together, after all), or maybe this arrangement was primarily done just for Ami’s sake; and, of course, there was also the consideration of Niki’s career, making her unable, as an idol, to openly be in a proper romantic relationship with anyone – but her decision to announce to the whole world that she is now dating her childhood friend, even knowing the insane public shitstorm it would create, is an act of burning bridges that *cannot* be ignored. It indicates that Niki is 100% serious about her intentions of pursuing Akira – to the point of even being willing to readily throw away her entire career for his sake – which immediately bumps her up in the “competing for Akira’s heart” rankings of from a mythical boogieman to an active apocalyptic-level threat, so the girls’ much more extreme reaction to the Instagram post compared to the news of them actually living together makes perfect logical sense to me.

spoilers.title: Ayane’s and Maya’s unnatural relationship with Ami
spoilers.html:
“Ayane and Maya are hanging out with Ami like they're all still friends and nothing's weird, even though she's been raping Maya, she made death threats to Ayane, and they both know she's "immortal". It's bizarrely out of character for Ayane to do nothing about a looming problem like this. She still hasn't even talked to Maya (that we've seen) even though it's obvious that Maya knows things that Ayane doesn't.”

I mean, even ignoring the fact that Ayane is still mostly mentally preoccupied with the aftermath of 0.53, constantly haunted by her lingering memories of Himawari to the point of being unable to properly focus on anything else, what *could* she even do about Ami? Talking to Sensei is out of the question (because of the explicit threat Ami made to her at the end of “The First Christmalloween”), and, to Ayane’s knowledge, no one else is actively aware of Ami’s true nature, so it’s not like she can just randomly ask Makoto (or any other member of RAS) for help with dealing with a murderous time-looper who can potentially force a Reset at any moment. Likewise, Maya is *also* currently preoccupied with her own stuff (trying to fix her deteriorating relationship with Akira, the Niki crisis, etcetera) and similarly doesn’t really have any good ideas for dealing with her “best friend”, and that is without even mentioning her weird inherent unconditional affection towards Ami (that was also shared by Maya Prime and is arguably hinted to be paranormal in nature).

Think of it this way: Ami, for all intents and purposes, is essentially an unstable time bomb – a bomb with a temporarily extinguished fuse (since, for whatever reason, she currently appears to be content with taking things slowly this cycle and just enjoying her day-to-day life to the fullest, with only some occasional “light mischief” like drugging Karin), but that is still ready to go off at a single wrong touch – and neither Maya nor Ayane really have any good ideas of how to even *begin* attempting to defuse her. So the best they can do is to kind of just… indefinitely stall for time, using this unexpected (but very welcome) lull to hopefully pacify Ami into even further inaction – especially since, once again, both girls presently have their plates full with a bunch of other personal stuff. Doing literally anything else – or, worse, actively provoking Ami – without *also* having a surefire way to deal with her if she decides to go ballistic is nothing short of suicidal, which is why their decision to continue keeping up the façade of a close-knit friend group (regardless of how these two truly feel about Arakawa junior) is a much safer and smarter approach, considering the alternatives.

spoilers.title: Nodoka
spoilers.html:
“Everything Nodoka has done in this game should have alienated her from the other girls: sexual harassment, sexual assault, ignoring boundaries, exposing secrets, unending condescension and self-superiority, and just never doing anything positive for anyone else. And yet, most everyone just ignores this and treats her like a normal friend/acquaintance. Sel needs victims for her to manipulate for her own storyline, so he has people go along with her for the flimsiest reasons. She's supposedly so good at manipulating people - is she really? We keep being told that, but I don't feel like we're shown it.”

I will address the first part of this criticism in the upcoming section on the topic of Sana’s actions in 0.49 (because my reasoning for both points is pretty much the same), and as for the second part, I assume that you are talking about Nodoka’s impromptu lingerie show that she organized in 0.58, in which case: is it really so inconceivable to assume that some (if not most) of the girls might be participating in Nodokathons *just* because they actually enjoy participating in Nodokathons, and not because Nodoka keeps somehow repeatedly manipulating them into it?

Because with the exception of the very first one, the last two events hosted by Nodoka have just been a completely natural extension of the regular Dorm Wars: just another contest where a bunch of girls have to compete with each other for Akira’s attention/validation, whether directly or indirectly, simply put to its logical extreme (that being sex) – and God knows that only, like, two or three girls in his entire class (Yumi, Io and maybe Yasu, none of whom notably ever took part in any of the Nodokathons – for obvious reasons) have to be actually persuaded into participating in Dorm Wars, while the rest of them do it 100% willingly, just because they like it. What makes Nodoka’s little gatherings any different?

As for her manipulation: I feel like we’ve seen plenty examples of it with just Akira alone, not to mention Yumi (“Matador”, “Things That Hurt” and “Twisting Ivy”) and Rin/Otoha (the 0.31 event chain that ends in “White-Fronted Parrot”, one of the main goals of which was to finally make those two have sex). Nodoka also managed to effortlessly navigate the mine field that is Ami after coming within an inch of being dismembered by her (Nodoka’s “How to Fuck Your Father” invite event chain), which is an achievement in and of itself, and I’m sure there are a few other instances of her playing the puppet-master that I am currently forgetting. And the Nodokathons, like I already mentioned earlier, can be mostly explained by the vast majority of the participants (with the exception of, like, Ayane for the second one, and possibly also Otoha in 0.58) being there 100% willingly, regardless of whether the reason for that is curiosity or depravity, and their personal feelings towards Nodoka herself don’t really matter in this particular case, since all of the girls are going there for *Akira*, not her: you can hate the organizer and still show up to the event itself, because the pros decidedly outweigh the cons here.

spoilers.title: Sana
spoilers.html:
“During Nodokathon 2, several of the girls saw Sana do something that really can't be described as anything other than pure evil. We got one scene of them expressing mild disappointment (while ignoring Molly's own role), and then everyone went back to hanging out with her and treating her creepy perversion like it's a bit of a joke. Ayane has some concerns, but she's barely even tried to talk to Sana, much less done anything about it.”

First of all, let’s look at *which* exact girls know about Sana’s actions. The initiator and enabler, Nodoka, obviously does not care, and neither does Ami – if anything, these two are actually fully supportive of Sana, because incest (duh). Ayane, on the contrary, clearly *does* care – in fact, she probably cares the most out of that entire group, partly out of genuine concern for Sara and partly out of her own personal hand-ups/projections regarding the subject of motherhood – but Ayane also has a bunch of other, much more pressing issues currently demanding her attention, many of which effectively coincided with the Sana/Sara situation time-wise, so for her it just became a matter of choosing your priorities (besides, if your only two other choices of friends are Ami and Maya, then Sana suddenly doesn’t seem like that bad of an option – at least when it comes to just wanting to take a break from all of the time-related stuff and simply hang out with someone you know and like). Miku is… honestly too selfish (and also too horny) to really care about anyone else’s issues aside from her own (and maybe Makoto’s), and Molly and Kirin are both in this weird position of actively having an ethical issue with what Sana did while simultaneously being self-aware enough to acknowledge that they are not that much better than her (Molly’s fantasies are only slightly less degenerate than Sana’s, and Kirin unambiguously wants to fuck her sister), to the point where neither girl really has a moral high ground to stand on without also coming off as a huge hypocrite.

So all in all, out of the six characters (among the active participants, excluding Sana herself) who are fully aware of what happened in “Thessalonians 4 (Lust Like the Pagans)”, there is essentially no one who would go as far as to completely break off their friendship with Sana just because of what she did, either because they fundamentally do not give a shit (Nodoka, Ami, Miku) or because there are extenuating circumstances that make a full-on condemnation of Sana very difficult, compared to just… continuing to occasionally hang out with her while keeping your true thoughts about the Sakakibara family to yourself (Ayane, Molly, Kirin).

And second of all (which also ties back to one of your earlier criticisms about Nodoka), we must further ask ourselves just how “moral” Akira’s class *actually* is, on average – compared to your normal highschooler, anyway – because I would fully argue that the (un)expected answer to that question is “not very”. Even ignoring extreme cases like Ami or Nodoka (and I guess post-awakening Sana) who are obviously in a league of their own as far as disregarding laws/morals goes, pretty much everyone in Akira’s entire class has actively done something openly amoral and/or illegal at one point or another, and that is without even mentioning the elephant in the room in how almost none of the girls see any issues with having romantic and/or sexual relationship with an adult man twice their age in a direct position of power over his students (with many of them even actively justifying it).

My point here – as someone who can personally relate to being just another bad person living among your fellow sinners, none of whom are any better than you (and many are way worse) – is that the notions of what is considered “acceptable” or “unacceptable” in such a group progressively get more and more blurry, and so do the limits of how much you yourself are actually willing to tolerate from your friends/acquaintances. So, as an outsider and a “good person”, it’s easy to look at something like Nodoka groping Makoto in the showers against her will or callously revealing the truth about Io (with zero regard to how Io herself feels about it) and wonder why anyone even bothers to speak with Nodoka anymore rather than immediately punching her on sight, but the ugly truth of it all is that it’s actually pretty easy to eventually reach a point where stuff like this goes from a total dealbreaker to “eh, well, I don’t really like it, but what can you do”. And the same goes for Kirin’s earlier actions towards Ayane, or Sana’s recent actions towards Sara – I knew people IRL who wouldn’t really bat an eye after learning details like this about someone, so LiL featuring a bunch of fucked up teenagers who are mostly isolated together from the rest of the world and also have a seemingly abnormal level of tolerance towards heinous/amoral actions doesn’t really strike me as strange, or even all that unrealistic.

(As a side note, I do fully understand that this just some random anecdotal evidence on my part and not really a proper logical argument, so if you still far from convinced and continue to persist in your belief that the girls should have had a much more severe reaction to Nodoka/Sana stuff, then I guess that is that – there is not much I can add to convince you otherwise.)

posts.content_html_raw:
aramaug said:
I really had to force my way through reading this update. I think it was my least favorite in the entire game. Compared to other contenders:
  • 0.39 (sports war) had "lol so random" humor that fell completely flat, and girls went along with whatever Nodoka wanted for incredibly flimsy reasons that contradict their own characters. This update had both of those things.
  • 0.50 (Nakayarakawayama beach trip) had Niki and Sara act in completely bizarre ways that seemed to retcon previous events. This update repeated that.
0.58 had another problem beyond the above: at times, the writing itself was really, really bad, even in serious events. Like, I have no idea how something like this made it past editing:
View attachment 6006465 View attachment 6006466
Or how about this bundle of cliches:
View attachment 6006491 View attachment 6006496 View attachment 6006498

Not to mention how little this feels like an actual character talking. I get there's a subtext here where Sara is trying to convince herself as much as Sensei, but it still sounds more like Selebus justifying her thought process to the reader.

A few quick thoughts on Niki:
- Did Niki ever acknowledge, even once, that grooming is a thing? She's acting like all these underage girls fell in love with Sensei and pursued him purely of their own volition. For some reason she encourages Rin and Chika's feelings without questioning where they come from. Even with Maya, who hints at how young she was, it's for some reason important to Niki that Maya "initiated" things. I expected her to have a very different reaction given what she thinks about Sekai.

- This to be in contention for dumbest line in the game:
View attachment 6006637 View attachment 6006638
We just got done with a whole arc where Niki was completely oblivious to things Sensei was doing in her own home, despite meeting many of the girls he was fucking. But now it just takes one look for her to figure it all out?

- I really have no idea what Selebus is trying to do with Niki's character at this point. Maya says something about her trying to find out how far Sensei has fallen to see if she can fix him, but in most of her interactions she seems very uninterested in learning. She explicitly tells Chika she doesn't care about her circumstances. It's like she's having these conversations with Rin and Chika just so she can... dispense relationship advice?

This update got me thinking about something that I think has a been a problem for a while: it often seems completely arbitrary which actions have massive consequences and which ones are completely forgotten, at least temporarily.
Many of the girls are treating Niki's instagram post and her involvement in Sensei's life like the Most Important Thing that ever happened. OK, fine, I can sort-of accept that, though it's weird that this provoked a much bigger reaction than Niki literally moving in with him (for the girls that knew about that).

But at the same time, this update was full of girls ignoring other really important things that have happened:

- Ayane and Maya are hanging out with Ami like they're all still friends and nothing's weird, even though she's been raping Maya, she made death threats to Ayane, and they both know she's "immortal". It's bizarrely out of character for Ayane to do nothing about a looming problem like this. She still hasn't even talked to Maya (that we've seen) even though it's obvious that Maya knows things that Ayane doesn't.

- Everything Nodoka has done in this game should have alienated her from the other girls: sexual harassment, sexual assault, ignoring boundaries, exposing secrets, unending condescension and self-superiority, and just never doing anything positive for anyone else. And yet, most everyone just ignores this and treats her like a normal friend/acquaintance. Sel needs victims for her to manipulate for her own storyline, so he has people go along with her for the flimsiest reasons. She's supposedly so good at manipulating people - is she really? We keep being told that, but I don't feel like we're shown it.

- During Nodokathon 2, several of the girls saw Sana do something that really can't be described as anything other than pure evil. We got one scene of them expressing mild disappointment (while ignoring Molly's own role), and then everyone went back to hanging out with her and treating her creepy perversion like it's a bit of a joke. Ayane has some concerns, but she's barely even tried to talk to Sana, much less done anything about it.

- Noriko continues to suffer no repercussions for the other way she betrayed Niki: she kept all of Sensei's crimes a secret, even as she watched her sister rebuild a relationship with a guy that Noriko knew was being unfaithful. She knows about the worst thing he's done (wizard Maya) and is still keeping that a secret, even though finding out later could potentially destroy Niki. At the very least, I would expect Noriko to struggle between her loyalty to Sensei and her loyalty to Niki, but if she feels any guilt about it the game has completely ignored it.

And this is supposed to be the same person?

I'm not sure I would consider this most recent update the worst (Nodokathon and death ball or whatever it was called probably still take the cake there), but things have definitely felt off with Niki's character fit a while now. Moments like glasswalker and Ayane epilogue give me hope, but poor writing over the last couple years really has me questioning if this is the same game it used to be.

Her being hypersexual is fine - whether it's the result of her trauma, external supernatural forces or both. And the latter was set up quite nicely to make her shift work narratively, the scenes themselves were excellent and the build-up was gradual with the major shift happening whilst Sensei was out of commission for months so that worked fine.

The issue is that for a significant chunk of the game there wasn't a single hint about this underlying issue, she comes across in the early chapters not only as disinterested in sex but wholly innocent of it, going so far as to be befuddled by the mere concept of lesbians. For the creator to pop up in discord at this point and explicitly state that she's been like this the whole time but was merely pretending to be innocent is pretty weak without any significant foreshadowing to that effect.

There are a few different aspects of Sana's character in Chapter 4 that I think people tend to confuse, but which we should really talk about separately.
  1. She has extreme kinks.
  2. She's constantly horny, to the extent that her whole life revolves around sex.
  3. She's no longer shy. She doesn't struggle with words, even around strangers. She's confident, shameless, and comes across as an exhibitionist despite claiming it isn't one of her kinks.
Of course there's some amount of correlation between these things, but they don't necessarily go together. You can be into freaky stuff without having a high sex drive. You can be both shy and a pervert.

Personally, I don't have a problem with #1. It wasn't made obvious in the early chapters, but that's consistent with Sana's personality - someone that reserved is going to hide her embarrassing traits, even from people she's close to. And there were some subtle clues. Here's an example from early in Chapter 2 where she gets excited by the idea of Sensei making her his property:

Narratively, #2 is explained by supernatural intervention. As shmurfer said, there were lots of signs that god(s) made her artificially horny throughout Chapter 3. Now the same thing is happening to Sara.


But I really don't like how far Selebus has taken it in Chapter 4. In Chapter 3, Sana was confused by what was happening and struggled against it. Now she's given in completely, with no reservations. There's no sign that she ever thought any other way, no second guessing "Should I really do this?" even if she ultimately decides "Yes, the new Sana takes what she wants." To me, it just reads like god has succeeded in overwriting her personality completely, and I don't find that interesting.


#3 is where Selebus completely loses me. People don't change that drastically and that suddenly, so the only way I can logically make sense of the new Sana is that she was only pretending to be shy for years, in order to hide her perversion. That's just comically nonsensical, and would invalidate pretty much her entire storyline for the first three chapters. A lot of her character arc is about learning to come out of her shell and overcome her shyness, but progress was slow.

Then suddenly a switch is flipped and she changes more off-screen between the end of Chapter 3 and the start of Chapter 4 than she did in the entirety of the first three chapters. I guess Selebus always meant for her to change in this way, but either he decided it was taking too long, or he realized he couldn't write the rest of her transformation arc in a convincing way, so he just tells the reader "Imagine that all happened while you weren't looking." It feels like the "draw the rest of the fucking owl" meme.
