But that doesn't tell us a lot about Akira's intentions, especially when these stories are coming from someone who was a young child at the time. He easily could have been grooming her for a relationship for a long time before it actually happened.
I think the new evidence suggests this wasn't the case, that Akira really did intend for his relationship with Maya to be innocent. In the memory, Akira says he can't let Maya come to his house because he has to hide her - he knows he's doing something very wrong and very illegal, and he has to keep it a secret. But this wasn't always the case, as he previously let her meet Ami and spend time at his house. To me, the obvious reason this changed is because of the start of their sexual relationship. Before that point, Akira didn't feel the need to hide her. Crucially, though, this also speaks to his intent; if he was always planning to turn the relationship sexual, he would have known from the beginning that he needed to keep it a secret.
So at the moment I lean toward the interpretation that Akira had good intentions for Maya, that he genuinely wanted to help a homeless girl, and things only went wrong after the accident broke him.
2. Akira's wish
From the way Himawari explained wishes that create people, my interpretation is that these wishes don't change the timeline (think also of how Kaori's wish added Nao to Sensei's timeline). So if Maya existed before the accident, Akira almost certainly wished for her before the accident (
Technically there's an alternative - Akira wishes for Maya after the accident, then sometime later the world resets to before the accident, bringing Maya along because she's now a permanent part of the world. But I have no idea why Sel would do that.
). That throws a wrench in the most popular theory of Akira's wish, that he was desperately lonely and/or horny after the accident and wished for a new (loli) girlfriend.
The stuff I wrote above about Akira's intentions also suggest that the wish wasn't sexual, though it's not conclusive. (We've seen with his treatment of Tsukasa that he's capable of consciously wanting to do the right thing at the same time that he grooms a wizard he's lusting for.) But I also tend to think a sexual wish is a lot less likely before the accident, when Akira is getting all he wants from two different "girlfriends".
I think it's more likely he was looking for someone to save. Hence Maya's backstory as a victim of abuse alone in the world. He sees himself in her and wants to save her the same way he credits Sekai with saving him - but only partially. Because while he loves Sekai for saving him from his abusive family and giving him something to live for, he also blames her for stealing his innocence/childhood. With Maya, he wanted to show that he could provide the good without the bad - but he failed.
I wonder if there's another element as well: maybe he wanted a "daughter" he could raise in place of his real one. It's very likely that Akira knew or at least heavily suspected that Ami was his biological daughter, but he didn't get to act like her father before the accident. (Ami has said she saw him occasionally back then, but they had no real relationship.) Maybe that was his choice, but I heavily doubt it - Akira's desire to be a father is a major aspect of his character (even if he also rejects it at times). He became a tutor and later a teacher because he wants to help kids.
So then why did he stay away from Ami? It seems to me that must have been Sekai's choice, that for whatever reason she wanted Ami to grow up with Nozomu very firmly in the father role. Akira may have desired that relationship and looked to Maya as a surrogate daughter. This could also play into why Narrator Ami thinks Maya stole her "story".

Surely she must have known why Ami was going to Akira's house, especially since he wasn't trying to hide Maya at that point. The exact nature of their relationship remains to be seen, but I think it's going to be important.

aramaug said:
I'm sure Nozomu didn't want Akira to act like a father to Ami, which would have played into things. But I think if Sekai really wanted it to happen, it would have. She was a very willful person and we know she was willing to defy Nozomu even when it got her a beating (e.g. by continuing to fuck Akira).

In the alternate timeline Nozomu is presumably completely out of the picture; Akira agreed to go to Kyoto, and Sekai married him instead. In the real timeline he wasn't willing to commit, which might have been what influenced Sekai's decision to let Nozomu raise Ami.

Some people wish for their perfect world. That creates a new world with new people that the wisher never gets to experience. Other people wish for a person or an object. It's my understanding those wishes add something to the wisher's already existing world. I wrote about this (with supporting screenshots) here.

As for wish people always existing, there's no hint that Nao-chan existed anywhere before she showed up in "First Contact". I think it's reasonable to assume Maya was the same, especially when New Maya has no memories whatsoever of her childhood before meeting Akira. I'm open to other arguments, though.
Click to expand...
I'm of the opinion that Nao isn't a wish, insomuch as she is some sort of God or Eldritch Creature.

Far too many weird things happen around her, she knows more than anyone else, and she has appeared to have powers on several occasions that no one else has had.

Her appearance as part of the Io Hole event, and the Chinami grooming event definitely point towards her not being human.

I am also running on the theory that the world we're experiencing is NOT the world created by Akira or Maya's wish, but instead by a series of wishes, including an overpowered wish made by Sekai.

If every wish granted creates a new world where that wish has always been true, then we get a central event. In this case, it's Sekai's death.

World 1: Sekai dies, Sensei wishes for Maya
World 2: Maya has always existed(Hence why she exists BEFORE Sekai dies). Sensei is a good teacher, hence why he tutors. Maya gets pregnant, which will ruin his life, so he kills himself. Maya wishes for Sensei to live.
World 3: Sekai(Who has now seen that Sensei is good with kids) makes a dying wish for Akira and her to have had a child(Ami) instead of her and Sensei's brother.
World 4: Ami is(cute) the central focus. Sekai's body is under the tree, and her organs are in Kaori, which gives more power to her wish, which is why the janitors can't wipe Ami once she gets her memories.(This could be the world we're experiencing)
(Potential World 5: Sensei in world 4 has made another wish, we just don't know it yet. Probably to have a massive cock, or something to do with being loved(seeing how easily everyone falls for him!))

We've seen several alternative timelines, one of which Ami is actually Sensei and Sekai's child, during which Sekai is still alive. I don't think that's a red herring, I think that's a massive hint to the world as we experience it.

A bit of a mess, but you get the gist. I think the wish mechanics are much deeper than we know as of yet, and that the timelooped world we see is caused by a cascade of wishes modifying the world in succession.

aramaug said:
There was a moment in 0.58 which I'm surprised no one has brought up for discussion, because I think it's a pretty big lore reveal: Maya's wizard memory (assuming it's genuine) confirmed that she met Ami back in the old district (at Akira's house, in fact).
Click to expand...
Another quality post that forces myself to iron my memory out!
Like you've implied, what is shown in Amplified Artistry! Drawing With Nao-chan! feels like the "based truth", as this isn't some second-handed knowledge retold by someone. It should be safe to confirm that Maya does know about Ami and has seen Ami since she was a wizard, but it's a good call to mention that wizard Maya never explicitly stated that she interacted with wizard Ami (and it didn't sound like that either) because it would have dramatically increased her chance being the mysterious playdate girl brought up in What Was, and inadvertently raised a really difficult question "When exactly did Maya show up in Akira's life? Before or after Sekai died?"
From these two lines of the same event, it should be evident that when this conversation happened, Sekai already died. However, how chronologically long between "wizard Maya seeing wizard Ami" and "this conversation" wasn't explicitly shown, so I'll put a pin in it despite feeling "not very long".
From this Maya event, however, it is really heavily implied that by the time Maya got spawned in and met Akira in the rain for the very first time, Sekai had already and simply died.
- "How it looked like you'd been crying".
- "Teach me all sorts of stuff about literature or poetry or any other pretentious bullshit that would help keep you distracted".
- At the same time, "you had a niece at home you were looking after".

Strictly speaking, the first one could be some subjective take on Maya's end and the latter two also never specified exactly when or much time has passed after that fateful night in the rain, but this entire confession does make it sound like all of the above happened in a quite quick and sequential way without an obvious gap that would suggest Sekai dying somewhere in between those Maya memories.

I am also considering these Maya's memories as undeniable truth because a) Nu Maya at that moment shouldn't have any reason to make up a story that also happens to fit other clues in prior chapters well, and b) a story direction of these memories being "divinely fake" for now is so BS that I would rather not think about it when I still have the chance.

Based on these, I would instead determine that "Maya and Akira before the accident" isn't a thing, without touching the more difficult questions like "what exactly was Akira's wish and how would a wish manifest in a different universe (chronological-wise)?" or "did Akira plan on going sexual with wizard Maya at the get-go because how secretive he was?", as I feel like the answer doesn't help decide whether Sekai died before or after Akira meeting Maya when everything else points at "before".

This would, however, also indirectly disprove the theory of Maya being the playdate girl because according to what Ami said, it would sound like Sekai was still alive and well at the time of the playdate. Therefore, one of the few following would have to be true:
1. Maya just wasn't the playdate girl. She saw Ami once but that was unplanned, was not THE playdate, and was something completely unrelated. Akira was likely smuggling watermelons from his current residence and wizard Maya just had to be a part of it then saw the red demon child herself.
2. Ami lied/misspoke/miscommunicated about this. That bitch.
3. Some Maya's memories are incorrect or fabricated and thus a good portion of this deduction becomes unreliable.
4. Selly screwed up and/or we just all misunderstood the guy. Maya WAS the playdate girl but the playdate was supposed to happen AFTER Sekai died and we simply got the wrong vibe from What Was.

Anyway, this is a rather interesting outcome honestly as I've also just assumed that Maya WAS the playdate girl until you pointed this out.

fdsasdf_p said:
Another quality post that forces myself to iron my memory out!
Like you've implied, what is shown in Amplified Artistry! Drawing With Nao-chan! feels like the "based truth", as this isn't some second-handed knowledge retold by someone. It should be safe to confirm that Maya does know about Ami and has seen Ami since she was a wizard, but it's a good call to mention that wizard Maya never explicitly stated that she interacted with wizard Ami (and it didn't sound like that either) because it would have dramatically increased her chance being the mysterious playdate girl brought up in What Was, and inadvertently raised a really difficult question "When exactly did Maya show up in Akira's life? Before or after Sekai died?"
From these two lines of the same event, it should be evident that when this conversation happened, Sekai already died. However, how chronologically long between "wizard Maya seeing wizard Ami" and "this conversation" wasn't explicitly shown, so I'll put a pin in it despite feeling "not very long".
View attachment 6142977 View attachment 6142975
From this Maya event, however, it is really heavily implied that by the time Maya got spawned in and met Akira in the rain for the very first time, Sekai had already and simply died.
- "How it looked like you'd been crying".
- "Teach me all sorts of stuff about literature or poetry or any other pretentious bullshit that would help keep you distracted".
- At the same time, "you had a niece at home you were looking after".
View attachment 6142620
View attachment 6142624
Strictly speaking, the first one could be some subjective take on Maya's end and the latter two also never specified exactly when or much time has passed after that fateful night in the rain, but this entire confession does make it sound like all of the above happened in a quite quick and sequential way without an obvious gap that would suggest Sekai dying somewhere in between those Maya memories.

I am also considering these Maya's memories as undeniable truth because a) Nu Maya at that moment shouldn't have any reason to make up a story that also happens to fit other clues in prior chapters well, and b) a story direction of these memories being "divinely fake" for now is so BS that I would rather not think about it when I still have the chance.
From Noriko's side of story from Loxosceles Reclusa, the order of events should be: Sekai died → Akira left the Nakayamas → Akira started tutoring wizard Noriko in the creepy apartment → It was only wizard Noriko plus other come-n-go girls for a while → Wizard Maya showed up.

Noriko's confession fits well with Maya's memories shown in Something to Do With Love or at least does not show blatant contradictions, and should place Sekai's death well after Maya's introduction to Akira's life.
Though it might make the "playdate girl == Maya" theory a lot more plausible, this also would imply that:
- Wizard Noriko would have meet Maya a lot sooner than she claimed, assuming Akira's old place being the same creepy apartment before and after Sekai's death, and there wasn't any secret door that delayed the meeting between these two pink/green nemesis.
- Wizard Maya would have died due to the lack of care when Akira became a veggie stick in his current residence and couldn't even take care of himself, let alone a secret wizard that he in theory hid from everyone.
Based on these, I would instead determine that "Maya and Akira before the accident" isn't a thing, without touching the more difficult questions like "what exactly was Akira's wish and how would a wish manifest in a different universe (chronological-wise)?" or "did Akira plan on going sexual with wizard Maya at the get-go because how secretive he was?", as I feel like the answer doesn't help decide whether Sekai died before or after Akira meeting Maya when everything else points at "before".

This would, however, also indirectly disprove the theory of Maya being the playdate girl because according to what Ami said, it would sound like Sekai was still alive and well at the time of the playdate. Therefore, one of the few following would have to be true:
1. Maya just wasn't the playdate girl. She saw Ami once but that was unplanned, was not THE playdate, and was something completely unrelated. Akira was likely smuggling watermelons from his current residence and wizard Maya just had to be a part of it then saw the red demon child herself.
2. Ami lied/misspoke/miscommunicated about this. That bitch.
3. Some Maya's memories are incorrect or fabricated and thus a good portion of this deduction becomes unreliable.
4. Selly screwed up and/or we just all misunderstood the guy. Maya WAS the playdate girl but the playdate was supposed to happen AFTER Sekai died and we simply got the wrong vibe from What Was.

Anyway, this is a rather interesting outcome honestly as I've also just assumed that Maya WAS the playdate girl until you pointed this out.
Click to expand...
Thanks for the reply, you raise some good counter-arguments.
Correct me if I'm wrong, but I don't think anyone has said Sensei tutored before the accident. That does raise the issue of what he did do for money, and why he would have the apartment if it wasn't for his work and he still had the "old house" (the one next door to Niki, I assume) where Ami had her play date. So maybe I'm wrong about this.

For Noriko specifically, she implied she saw him at her house before the accident, but the tutoring only started later (long enough after the accident that he was interacting with the world again).

So here's what I'm imagining:
1. Akira meets Maya and takes her in.
2. The accident happens.
3. Akira is taking care of Ami and Maya separately, and at some point starts a sexual relationship with Maya.
4. He realizes he needs money and decides tutoring is the solution.
5. The apartment is the ideal location for tutoring, but at this point he's in "hide Maya" mode, so he arranges for her to be elsewhere during his tutoring hours. (Which probably means sending an 8-year-old out to spend time in the city unsupervised, but hey, nobody ever said he's the most responsible parent.)
6. He continues to teach Maya in private as well. At some point he realizes that Maya and Noriko are far more intellectually advanced than his other students, and it will help both of their development if he teaches them together.
7. He arranges for Maya to show up to tutoring as a completely new student, as far as Noriko is concerned.

Of course, there's no direct evidence for any of this, so you're right to be skeptical. And I'm just now realizing that Maya's story in "Something to Do With Love" implies that she met Noriko before the sexual relationship started, which throws a wrench into things.
There's a lot to unpack here. I definitely agree with you that, taken in isolation, this passage points strongly at a post-accident meeting. I'm not sure it completely rules out the alternative, though.

1. Maya opens by saying there was a bed in the apartment, but he went out and bought a futon. Later she says he never spent the night. That could suggest that time passed in between the two - originally he slept at the apartment, but that stopped when he had to start taking care of Ami.

2. It seems to me that this story contradicts the "Drawing with Nao-chan" memory no matter what. Akira is already in "hide Maya" mode in this story, but she doesn't know about Ami until he tells her. In the "Drawing with Nao-chan" memory, she says that she learned about Ami before he felt the need to start hiding her (or at least before he felt letting her into his house was dangerous). So this has me thinking that New Maya's memory is faulty, and I'm wondering what else she got wrong.

3. Akira crying when they met is certainly more likely after the accident, but he had plenty to be unhappy about beforehand as well. He's in an ongoing relationship with his sexual abuser, who also fucks his brother he hates who physically abused/abuses the two of them. He's also hiding all that from his actual girlfriend.

Completely off-topic thought: reading this passage, it occurs to me how similar New Maya's first memory is to the first meeting with Nao-chan ("First Contact"): in both cases Sensei finds a girl sleeping on the ground in the rain, and Sensei/Kaori decides to help the girl after discovering they have no family and no place to go. There's a parallel in how each of them met the girl they wished for, which might further suggest that these are the moments in which Maya/Nao were created for them.
Your post brought up another question I'd like to discuss - in the memory, when Maya says "[Ami is] pretty. But I won't say anymore than that because I don't want to hurt your feelings." what is she alluding to? What might she have said that would hurt his feelings?

My original thoughts was that she could have said "She looks nothing like you." But I'm not sure how much sense that makes, either as a comment or as a cause of emotional pain, unless both Maya and Akira know that she's Akira's daughter.

A new idea that occurs to me now: what if it was "She looks like her mother"? I think that makes a lot of sense, as any reference to Sekai will be painful to Akira, but it requires that Maya knows what Sekai looks like. And I think that's only possible if she was around before the accident (Afterwards Akira got rid of pictures of Sekai along with everything else that reminded him of her).

Any other ideas?

spoilers.title: Noriko
spoilers.html:
Correct me if I'm wrong, but I don't think anyone has said Sensei tutored before the accident. That does raise the issue of what he did do for money, and why he would have the apartment if it wasn't for his work and he still had the "old house" (the one next door to Niki, I assume) where Ami had her play date. So maybe I'm wrong about this.

For Noriko specifically, she implied she saw him at her house before the accident, but the tutoring only started later (long enough after the accident that he was interacting with the world again).

So here's what I'm imagining:
1. Akira meets Maya and takes her in.
2. The accident happens.
3. Akira is taking care of Ami and Maya separately, and at some point starts a sexual relationship with Maya.
4. He realizes he needs money and decides tutoring is the solution.
5. The apartment is the ideal location for tutoring, but at this point he's in "hide Maya" mode, so he arranges for her to be elsewhere during his tutoring hours. (Which probably means sending an 8-year-old out to spend time in the city unsupervised, but hey, nobody ever said he's the most responsible parent.)
6. He continues to teach Maya in private as well. At some point he realizes that Maya and Noriko are far more intellectually advanced than his other students, and it will help both of their development if he teaches them together.
7. He arranges for Maya to show up to tutoring as a completely new student, as far as Noriko is concerned.

Of course, there's no direct evidence for any of this, so you're right to be skeptical. And I'm just now realizing that Maya's story in "Something to Do With Love" implies that she met Noriko before the sexual relationship started, which throws a wrench into things.

spoilers.title: What Is
Something to Do With Love
spoilers.html:
There's a lot to unpack here. I definitely agree with you that, taken in isolation, this passage points strongly at a post-accident meeting. I'm not sure it completely rules out the alternative, though.

1. Maya opens by saying there was a bed in the apartment, but he went out and bought a futon. Later she says he never spent the night. That could suggest that time passed in between the two - originally he slept at the apartment, but that stopped when he had to start taking care of Ami.

2. It seems to me that this story contradicts the "Drawing with Nao-chan" memory no matter what. Akira is already in "hide Maya" mode in this story, but she doesn't know about Ami until he tells her. In the "Drawing with Nao-chan" memory, she says that she learned about Ami before he felt the need to start hiding her (or at least before he felt letting her into his house was dangerous). So this has me thinking that New Maya's memory is faulty, and I'm wondering what else she got wrong.

3. Akira crying when they met is certainly more likely after the accident, but he had plenty to be unhappy about beforehand as well. He's in an ongoing relationship with his sexual abuser, who also fucks his brother he hates who physically abused/abuses the two of them. He's also hiding all that from his actual girlfriend.

Completely off-topic thought: reading this passage, it occurs to me how similar New Maya's first memory is to the first meeting with Nao-chan ("First Contact"): in both cases Sensei finds a girl sleeping on the ground in the rain, and Sensei/Kaori decides to help the girl after discovering they have no family and no place to go. There's a parallel in how each of them met the girl they wished for, which might further suggest that these are the moments in which Maya/Nao were created for them.

Hello everyone, I'm a new player. I just finished the latest content of this work a few days ago and came up with some ideas. I think they are interesting and would like to discuss whether these ideas are reasonable.

Since my native language is not English, some of the following content was translated with the help of AI. Please forgive me.

It is known that this world setting has a "Wishing" mechanism. Based on the hints from 0.53, I think wishing has a monkey's paw effect—wishes can be misinterpreted, or require paying a painful price. Moreover, whether one has made a wish or has a tendency to wish is closely related to "whether one can normally communicate about the apocalypse phenomenon".

Based on this conjecture, I think the people who "can communicate normally" all satisfy this conjecture. Let me list them below:

Akira: Created Maya / (Because there are too many possible "side effect" options for him, this point can't be fully determined yet)

Maya: Created this world / The price is being unable to express her feelings to Akira

Ayane: Resolved the conflict between her "wanting a child" and Akira's "not wanting a child" / The price was Hima disappearing

Makoto: Found a world where she can do as she pleases / The price was her father's death

Yumi: Mother-daughter reconciliation / The price was Yuki getting cancer

Tsuneyo: Father healed (or resurrected?) / The price was her father looking very strange

Sana: Became good at communication (or "the teacher fell in love with me") / Her price might be that her personality has become very terrible now, or the price has yet to manifest. I think at the end of Chapter 4, something else will happen to her.

Sara: Revived her son / The price is that her son is only a ghost, and she herself experiences "blackouts" like Akira.

Futaba: Wanted a better-looking version of herself / The price was that two Futabas appeared during the eighth reset (though it's still unclear if she can communicate normally)

Uta: Wished that the past photo-taking incident never happened / The price is unknown (her wish wasn't properly fulfilled; in version 0.57 she was persuaded by Sekai and withdrew her wish)

Sekai: Wanted to be with her beloved forever / The price was that she possessed Kaori, became a "vessel" for the deity, split into multiple Sekais, and became a ghost.

Nodoka: Wished for her mother's return / The price is that her mother ignores her, or her mother remains in a constant state of "blackouts".

Ami's situation is very special. I suspect that Ami's wish actually worked together with Maya's wish to create this world. This might explain why Ami, like Maya, possesses many "privileges". However, the price she paid is still unclear.

There is another questionable point: if Nodoka herself is a product of a wish, then logically she should not have the ability to make wishes, which might be a bit confusing logically.

The above is just a brief expression of some thoughts of mine. Actually, there are many more details, and I can also find some relevant evidence.

I also have some other speculations, such as: "Wishing requires going onto the rooftop, but the wisher will subsequently forget about it"; "What Hima and one of the Sekais are currently doing, and what Akira needs to do in the future, might be stopping or withdrawing the wishes previously made by the characters."
If you have any insights about my ideas, you are very welcome to discuss with me. I will keep an eye on this thread. Thank you in advance for your reply!!!

It is known that this world setting has a "Wishing" mechanism. Based on the hints from 0.53, I think wishing has a monkey's paw effect—wishes can be misinterpreted, or require paying a painful price. Moreover, whether one has made a wish or has a tendency to wish is closely related to "whether one can normally communicate about the apocalypse phenomenon".

Based on this conjecture, I think the people who "can communicate normally" all satisfy this conjecture. Let me list them below:

Akira: Created Maya / (Because there are too many possible "side effect" options for him, this point can't be fully determined yet)

Maya: Created this world / The price is being unable to express her feelings to Akira

Ayane: Resolved the conflict between her "wanting a child" and Akira's "not wanting a child" / The price was Hima disappearing

Makoto: Found a world where she can do as she pleases / The price was her father's death

Yumi: Mother-daughter reconciliation / The price was Yuki getting cancer

Tsuneyo: Father healed (or resurrected?) / The price was her father looking very strange

Sana: Became good at communication (or "the teacher fell in love with me") / Her price might be that her personality has become very terrible now, or the price has yet to manifest. I think at the end of Chapter 4, something else will happen to her.

Sara: Revived her son / The price is that her son is only a ghost, and she herself experiences "blackouts" like Akira.

Futaba: Wanted a better-looking version of herself / The price was that two Futabas appeared during the eighth reset (though it's still unclear if she can communicate normally)

Uta: Wished that the past photo-taking incident never happened / The price is unknown (her wish wasn't properly fulfilled; in version 0.57 she was persuaded by Sekai and withdrew her wish)

Sekai: Wanted to be with her beloved forever / The price was that she possessed Kaori, became a "vessel" for the deity, split into multiple Sekais, and became a ghost.

Nodoka: Wished for her mother's return / The price is that her mother ignores her, or her mother remains in a constant state of "blackouts".

Ami's situation is very special. I suspect that Ami's wish actually worked together with Maya's wish to create this world. This might explain why Ami, like Maya, possesses many "privileges". However, the price she paid is still unclear.

There is another questionable point: if Nodoka herself is a product of a wish, then logically she should not have the ability to make wishes, which might be a bit confusing logically.

The above is just a brief expression of some thoughts of mine. Actually, there are many more details, and I can also find some relevant evidence.

I also have some other speculations, such as: "Wishing requires going onto the rooftop, but the wisher will subsequently forget about it"; "What Hima and one of the Sekais are currently doing, and what Akira needs to do in the future, might be stopping or withdrawing the wishes previously made by the characters."
Click to expand...
I've been summoned to reply since this person has absolutely god-tier taste in profile image.
I don't recall anyone working that far into the idea of a monkey's paw (the idea itself has been mentioned but not to this degree), and I like it. I was able to understand your post without issues, but I'll summarize for those that may have issues:

Their idea is that everyone involved in Terminal 23, aka main characters, may be there because of a wish - and that wish ends up, as much as a "monkey's paw" or a "genie's wish", being counter-intuitive to what they want. For instance, Yumi wished for a mother-daughter relationship, but the offset is that Yuki gets cancer. I think the examples given were quite interesting, and I suggest people read them in the original post.
Tbh I think it's one of those cases that what you suggested is better than what Selebus thought of, but if this is indeed the case it would be great. A couple of issues with this being the case are that

1. Wishes are granted to other versions of yourself that were not the ones that made the wish. This is a rule that Selebus established that made everything convoluted (so far for no reason that I can see, since the one example of a wish that we have is the exception for that rule = Maya's world).

2. Following "1", Maya herself is a wish from Akira, suggested to be from an Akira that shouldn't have met her. But, more importantly, a wish shouldn't have been able to get a wish granted, much less herself be able to get said wish, instead of a parallel version of Maya that never wished for it. The whole thing is very convoluted (both Akira and Maya's situations) and that makes it hard to properly have a baseline to understanding the "normal" wishing system.

3. Himawari shouldn't be able to be a wish, because Himawari used her wish - and from her monologue about the system, she does not refer to herself as an exception. Furthermore, if she was also a wish that was able to make a wish, then it would follow that everyone would observe her same as Maya, but no such thing seems to have taken place.

Now, not issues, but just things I'd like to add:

A. The topic of wishing on a rooftop, in fact, the whole idea of a reset being a wish has been discussed a lot and the consensus is that it is highly likely that the process to reset involves making a wish. The idea of Maya Prime praying in order to reset the world (praying is just wishing for something from a god), and, ironically, we sort of got confirmation for that from the non-canonical original fanfest series, when the girls develop a rotation where each one can define the next reset conditions through wishes.

B. The one thing is that wishing in the sense of Maya creating a world, or Akira creating Maya, does not seem to be the same thing as wishing for a reset. The reason I say this is because the reset itself seems to be a regular system for the parallel worlds, as explained by Himawari. It's just that Terminal 23 has to be reset constantly due to its very nature being broken. But other worlds also have to be reset from time to time. Thus, I interpret the wishing for the reset as more of a [system command], rather than a proper wish. Furthermore, each person can only use one "world creating wish", as it is a pact with a god, and yet resets happen all the time.

C. One last thing I'd like to add is that I find your idea of something being lost very appealing in terms of the wish. Again, I suspect your idea is more developed and intriguing than what Selebus cooked up - but so far he explains that what the god gets from the wish contract is simply validation of its existence as a wish granter. I find this acceptable as an explanation, but I prefer your idea of something actually being taken from the person - in this case, the "loop in the hole", the hidden trap in their perfect wish.

*The explanation of getting validation comes from Pareidolia, even though Pegasus seems intent on taking something from Sana. So there is a contradiction even in what we have.
All in all, great contribution and welcome to the thread.

spoilers.title: Monkey's paw and Wishing theories.
spoilers.html:
It is known that this world setting has a "Wishing" mechanism. Based on the hints from 0.53, I think wishing has a monkey's paw effect—wishes can be misinterpreted, or require paying a painful price. Moreover, whether one has made a wish or has a tendency to wish is closely related to "whether one can normally communicate about the apocalypse phenomenon".

Based on this conjecture, I think the people who "can communicate normally" all satisfy this conjecture. Let me list them below:

Akira: Created Maya / (Because there are too many possible "side effect" options for him, this point can't be fully determined yet)

Maya: Created this world / The price is being unable to express her feelings to Akira

Ayane: Resolved the conflict between her "wanting a child" and Akira's "not wanting a child" / The price was Hima disappearing

Makoto: Found a world where she can do as she pleases / The price was her father's death

Yumi: Mother-daughter reconciliation / The price was Yuki getting cancer

Tsuneyo: Father healed (or resurrected?) / The price was her father looking very strange

Sana: Became good at communication (or "the teacher fell in love with me") / Her price might be that her personality has become very terrible now, or the price has yet to manifest. I think at the end of Chapter 4, something else will happen to her.

Sara: Revived her son / The price is that her son is only a ghost, and she herself experiences "blackouts" like Akira.

Futaba: Wanted a better-looking version of herself / The price was that two Futabas appeared during the eighth reset (though it's still unclear if she can communicate normally)

Uta: Wished that the past photo-taking incident never happened / The price is unknown (her wish wasn't properly fulfilled; in version 0.57 she was persuaded by Sekai and withdrew her wish)

Sekai: Wanted to be with her beloved forever / The price was that she possessed Kaori, became a "vessel" for the deity, split into multiple Sekais, and became a ghost.

Nodoka: Wished for her mother's return / The price is that her mother ignores her, or her mother remains in a constant state of "blackouts".

Ami's situation is very special. I suspect that Ami's wish actually worked together with Maya's wish to create this world. This might explain why Ami, like Maya, possesses many "privileges". However, the price she paid is still unclear.

There is another questionable point: if Nodoka herself is a product of a wish, then logically she should not have the ability to make wishes, which might be a bit confusing logically.

The above is just a brief expression of some thoughts of mine. Actually, there are many more details, and I can also find some relevant evidence.

I also have some other speculations, such as: "Wishing requires going onto the rooftop, but the wisher will subsequently forget about it"; "What Hima and one of the Sekais are currently doing, and what Akira needs to do in the future, might be stopping or withdrawing the wishes previously made by the characters."

my thoughts
spoilers.html:
Tbh I think it's one of those cases that what you suggested is better than what Selebus thought of, but if this is indeed the case it would be great. A couple of issues with this being the case are that

1. Wishes are granted to other versions of yourself that were not the ones that made the wish. This is a rule that Selebus established that made everything convoluted (so far for no reason that I can see, since the one example of a wish that we have is the exception for that rule = Maya's world).

2. Following "1", Maya herself is a wish from Akira, suggested to be from an Akira that shouldn't have met her. But, more importantly, a wish shouldn't have been able to get a wish granted, much less herself be able to get said wish, instead of a parallel version of Maya that never wished for it. The whole thing is very convoluted (both Akira and Maya's situations) and that makes it hard to properly have a baseline to understanding the "normal" wishing system.

3. Himawari shouldn't be able to be a wish, because Himawari used her wish - and from her monologue about the system, she does not refer to herself as an exception. Furthermore, if she was also a wish that was able to make a wish, then it would follow that everyone would observe her same as Maya, but no such thing seems to have taken place.

Now, not issues, but just things I'd like to add:

A. The topic of wishing on a rooftop, in fact, the whole idea of a reset being a wish has been discussed a lot and the consensus is that it is highly likely that the process to reset involves making a wish. The idea of Maya Prime praying in order to reset the world (praying is just wishing for something from a god), and, ironically, we sort of got confirmation for that from the non-canonical original fanfest series, when the girls develop a rotation where each one can define the next reset conditions through wishes.

B. The one thing is that wishing in the sense of Maya creating a world, or Akira creating Maya, does not seem to be the same thing as wishing for a reset. The reason I say this is because the reset itself seems to be a regular system for the parallel worlds, as explained by Himawari. It's just that Terminal 23 has to be reset constantly due to its very nature being broken. But other worlds also have to be reset from time to time. Thus, I interpret the wishing for the reset as more of a [system command], rather than a proper wish. Furthermore, each person can only use one "world creating wish", as it is a pact with a god, and yet resets happen all the time.

C. One last thing I'd like to add is that I find your idea of something being lost very appealing in terms of the wish. Again, I suspect your idea is more developed and intriguing than what Selebus cooked up - but so far he explains that what the god gets from the wish contract is simply validation of its existence as a wish granter. I find this acceptable as an explanation, but I prefer your idea of something actually being taken from the person - in this case, the "loop in the hole", the hidden trap in their perfect wish.

*The explanation of getting validation comes from Pareidolia, even though Pegasus seems intent on taking something from Sana. So there is a contradiction even in what we have.

haha, first of all, I really appreciate your patient and enthusiastic reply.

I initially didn't notice that Hima said wishing can only wish for "people" or "world", hah.... however, I think Hima is hiding a lot of things and not telling, or she simply doesn't know.

I still think the characters can wish for "an event", which might be related to the deity in the story. Otherwise, it would never explain why Hima disappeared after Ayane got pregnant.

And my idea is that these wishes are generated "during the story", rather than being predetermined from the beginning. The characters developed some wishes in the story, and then there is a power that "kindly" helps the characters fulfill them.
I'll give a few examples in a bit more detail to show that these are not simply turning "good" to "bad", but "fulfilling the wish in a terrible way".

For example, Ayane. What I want to say is that Ayane found out she was pregnant before the third reset, and then she was very depressed inside because she was troubled by the conflict between her "wanting a child" and Akira's "not wanting a child". Eventually Hima disappeared, and this conflict was "resolved". So Hima herself is not a product of a wish; she can wish, but in the current world her existence was concealed due to Ayane's wish.

For example, Makoto. She has a certain chronic depression, and inside she just longs for a carefree life. With a bit of an Electra complex, her almost self-tormenting diligence was merely to respond to certain expectations. In the end, her father's death finally snapped the taut string in her heart. She finally has a reason to escape that kind of self-oppressive life. It's just, you know, her father died.

For example, Yumi. After learning that her mother had quit drugs and was working normally, she may have also sought mother-daughter reconciliation in her heart. Looking at the stories of Yumi and Yuki, you can clearly see that "Yuki getting cancer" greatly pushed forward the reconciliation between Yumi and Yuki. It's just, you know, Yuki got cancer.

Let me talk about a more recent version, an event involving Uta and Sekai that left a deep impression on me. After Akira told Uta about the time loop, Uta went into heat as if possessed. Although she realized there was a loop, she didn't particularly care—this might be another form of "suppression effect"—however, I guess it might be that after Niki's official announcement, it greatly heightened Uta's sense of crisis (after all, she is a "monogamist" who doesn't even want to share Akira with Io), which prompted her to make this wish. This phenomenon is very, very similar to what is happening with Ami and Sana now, but this time Sekai stopped her.

(There's another point worth mentioning: the phone rang for a long time before Uta checked it, but compared to the earlier event between Akira and Uta at the love hotel, she was very sensitive to phone messages. Although it could also be said that Uta's relationship with Akira has deepened, making her a bit "reckless," Sekai later hinted at this as well. )


I'm trying to be as brief as possible, for fear of taking up too much of your time. However, you can see that in the similar events involving Sekai with Tsuneyo and Uta, Sekai's goals are completely opposite. I have reason to believe these are two different Sekais; perhaps they belong to two different factions, one wanting Akira to leave, and the other hoping Akira will stay here forever. In the Uta event, Sekai not only abstractly explained the nature of the world to her, but also emphasized to her "you're not the type to ever be that assertive and open about your sexual needs". Finally, she considerately said "make yourself important" and meaningfully "help lay me to rest". At the very least, we can believe that this Sekai is "not bad", so the act of "stopping Uta" is also "not bad".
There are too many things like this. Of course, it's very likely that what I'm thinking is different from what Sel has in mind. What I'm saying is not to justify some strange plot choices by Sel, but to provide a relatively interesting perspective to re-examine the story. If events like Yuki getting cancer and the news of Makoto's father's death, which happened so abruptly, were just used to create some sensational elements, the plot would be... truly terrible by today's standards. I can't say that Sel can handle all of this perfectly, so I'm just skeptical.

Finally, thank you again for your reply. Bro, your profile picture is also really, really great.

B. The one thing is that wishing in the sense of Maya creating a world, or Akira creating Maya, does not seem to be the same thing as wishing for a reset. The reason I say this is because the reset itself seems to be a regular system for the parallel worlds, as explained by Himawari. It's just that Terminal 23 has to be reset constantly due to its very nature being broken. But other worlds also have to be reset from time to time. Thus, I interpret the wishing for the reset as more of a [system command], rather than a proper wish. Furthermore, each person can only use one "world creating wish", as it is a pact with a god, and yet resets happen all the time.

posts.content_html_raw: Okay, so about the Yuki rape thing. I'm not trying to glaze Sel here but I will say one thing. People are fucking stubborn sometimes. For Yuki she said before the event that she's at rock bottom but she's been on rock bottom before. She said that Akira seeing her getting her shit together was one of the only times in her life that she wasn't at rock bottom. So getting back on drugs and dropping out of work and dipping isn't anything new for her. But she wasn't going to change. She wasn't going to accept help if it meant just letting everyone down AGAIN. How does someone who's used to rock bottom get a wake up call? Drop them more. Not good logic for having a gang rape scene I know but to me it felt like the only thing that would actually make this person go "Yeah this sucks and putting in the effort to get better sounds like a daunting task but it sure beats THIS". By rule of comparison being Tsubasa's personal plaything seems fucking dandy. If there was ever a reason to accept that scene exists, for me. It's that.

posts.content_html_raw:
I don't think that's the main issue, but the handling of it. One can agree or not that the rape was necessary "for character development" or what have you. But what about what came later? We can have the rape being shown, but we can't have the so-called revenge? Why? The one mention about it has to be a joke?
This is already a repeated cycle from Selebus where he pulls traumatic shit and doesn't follow up. Nodoka sexually assaulted Yumi (to varying degrees), and everyone turned against Yumi when she punched Nodoka lights out for it. Then after years of anticipating if it would ever get revealed to either everyone or just Futaba the why of the situation we got nothing. People more or less got to the conclusion of "man, Nodoka is shitty, maybe there was something more to it" and that was it.

The whole Futaba and Nodoka situation with the book? Same thing. Futaba got "super mad" but then she remembered that Nodoka is such a rascal and we got nothing from it either. Can't shake up the status quo that much I guess.

Obviously none of it came to this degree of brutality (while not being related to reset/god magic).
I talked about it a lot in an old post already:
Moonflare said:
A lot of people talk about "stomachache" but I dread having to rewatch Yuki getting gangraped for absolutely no reason just so that she can get a different hair color, and Tsubasa saying later that "she may have cut the dick off of everyone that raped her" off-camera.

Well, how? Didn't she state that she kept the distance from Yakuza? But now she cut the dicks out of all the top lieutenants of it? What about Yumi's father? What did she do to him? Absolutely pathetic follow-up to a deeply traumatic scene. Makes no sense. If this was to be the resolution, why go that far?

I really like Yuki and the payoff for including this was absolutely not worth it for me. She already had cancer. Her past had already been stated enough with the blowjob alone. They could have just refused to pay her anyway and thrown her out. I do not agree with Selebus choices past that point. Absolute low point of the chapter (if not the game) for me.
It really pisses me off when an author writes something deeply traumatic to a character I love, and either there's no revenge or they don't show it.
Click to expand...
For an example of how I wish it was handled, take Niki's situation. While I think Akira reenacting sixteen candles is way too silly and simple of a resolution
it has extensive follow-up. Niki talks and vents about what happened to other people, we SEE her talking and digesting what happened. We see the actions she takes and how it affects people around her. And sorry, but seeing your boyfriend banging your little sister is nowhere near as traumatic as being gangraped for cash, not receiving said cash, then being thrown out naked in the street.

At the end of the day, Yuki is a side character, and the event itself is not directly related to Akira, thus she gets sub-par treatment on the follow-up. Furthermore, she's not actively romantically involved with Akira, which I think also gave Selebus leeway to do what he did to her (not that I agree with it). But that's how I see it.
